title: Objectivity
summary: Volitional adherence to reality by the method of logic. Knowledge as contextual and hierarchical.

lessons.title: Adherence to reality
lessons.objective: State objectivity as a chosen adherence to the facts, not as neutrality and not as a mind that writes reality.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is objectivity?

choices.text: Volitional adherence to reality by the method of logic
Having no values and taking no stand
Agreeing with whatever most people report
Letting a feeling decide what is real

feedback.note: Objectivity names a method of sticking to the facts, not a mood of indifference.

exercises.prompt: What does adherence point at?

choices.text: Reality, the facts as they are
Whatever one wishes were true
The approval of a group
A preferred style of speaking

feedback.note: To adhere is to keep one's conclusions tied to reality rather than to wishes.

exercises.prompt: Match each slogan to the idea it actually names.

pairs.left: Stick to the facts by a method
Refuse every evaluation
Let consciousness invent the facts
Skip any method and claim the facts just announce themselves

feedback.note: Objectivity needs both reality and a method of knowing it. Neutrality, subjectivism, and intrinsicism each drop one side of that pair.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit's name for objectivity.

feedback.note: The thing one adheres to is reality. Fashion, consensus, and feeling are not substitutes for it.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition in the order this unit uses.

feedback.note: The three parts are the choice to adhere, the reality one adheres to, and logic as the method.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, I am objective because I care about nothing. What is wrong with that?

choices.text: Objectivity is adherence to facts, not an absence of concern
Nothing is wrong; indifference is the method
It fails only if the person still has a favorite color
It fails only because the sentence was spoken aloud

feedback.note: Caring about a fact is compatible with objectivity. Dropping the facts in the name of neutrality is not.

exercises.prompt: Which claim treats consciousness as the author of reality?

choices.text: If I refuse to believe it, it is not a fact
I have to look before I conclude
A fact stays a fact when I dislike it
I check a claim against the evidence

feedback.note: Subjectivism puts the mind in charge of what exists. Objectivity keeps the facts in charge of the conclusion.

exercises.prompt: Match the mistake to what it drops.

pairs.left: My wish settles the fact
pairs.right: Reality as independent of the wish

pairs.left: No method is needed; truth just shines
I will not take sides, so I will not look

feedback.note: Each mistake abandons one part of objectivity: the facts, the method, or the choice to adhere.

exercises.prompt: Objectivity is not a mind writing the world. It is adherence to what?

feedback.note: Wishes, slogans, and moods can be real events in a mind. They do not replace the facts one is judging.

exercises.prompt: Put the objective order of judgment together.

tokens.text: then rewrite them to fit a wish

feedback.note: The facts come first. Identification follows them. Rewriting or ignoring them is the opposite of adherence.

lessons.title: The method of logic
lessons.objective: Identify logic as the method of objectivity: non-contradictory identification of the facts.

exercises.prompt: What method does objectivity use?

choices.text: Logic, non-contradictory identification
Faith in an authority
A poll of opinions
An unchecked hunch

feedback.note: Logic is the method named in this unit. Faith, polls, and hunches are not that method.

exercises.prompt: Non-contradictory identification means which of these?

choices.text: Name what is, and do not treat it as also not that
Call the same fact true and false at once when that is convenient
Skip identification and keep only a feeling
Rename a contradiction so it sounds peaceful

feedback.note: Logic keeps an identification consistent with the identity of what is identified.

exercises.prompt: Match each practice to its place in the method.

pairs.left: State what a thing is
Reject calling it both A and non-A
Use that pair as the way of knowing

feedback.note: Logic is not a separate world of symbols. It is identification kept free of contradiction.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two words this unit uses for the method.

feedback.note: The method is non-contradictory identification. Arbitrary assertion and revelation are not logic.

exercises.prompt: Order the method as this unit states it.

feedback.note: Adherence is not a blank stare. The method that carries it out is logic.

exercises.prompt: A report says the device is both fully on and fully off in the same respect at the same time. What does logic require?

choices.text: Treat that as a failed identification and sort out the facts
Keep both claims because contradiction is deeper truth
Ask which claim has more friends
Pick the claim that feels calmer

feedback.note: A contradiction is a sign that identification has gone wrong, not a special kind of fact.

exercises.prompt: Why is logic called a method here, not a substitute for looking?

choices.text: It is the way one identifies facts, not a source that replaces them
It lets one skip the facts and still be objective
It is a set of answers one is born already knowing
It is only a custom about polite debate

feedback.note: Logic processes what one has observed. It does not manufacture observations.

exercises.prompt: Match the move to whether it follows the method.

pairs.left: Integrate two observations without contradiction
Assert both a claim and its denial
Drop an observation because it is inconvenient

feedback.note: The method both identifies and refuses contradiction. Dropping an inconvenient fact fails adherence even before the contradiction is named.

exercises.prompt: Complete the relation of logic to objectivity.

feedback.note: Without logic, adherence has no method. Logic is not the rival of objectivity.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses the method?

choices.text: The reading and the theory must be brought into one non-contradictory account
I will believe both the reading and its denial
I will believe whichever line I heard last
I will not identify anything, so I cannot be wrong

feedback.note: Refusing to identify is not a safe form of logic. The method is identification without contradiction.

lessons.title: A choice to adhere
lessons.objective: Separate what is given in awareness from the choice to adhere to it by logic.

exercises.prompt: Why does this unit call adherence volitional?

choices.text: One can choose to follow the facts by logic or to evade them
Every conclusion forms itself with no choice involved
Only muscles can be moved; thinking cannot be chosen
Objectivity arrives by luck and cannot be practiced

feedback.note: Volitional means the adherence is up to the person. It is not an automatic stamp on every thought.

exercises.prompt: What is not a matter of choosing the content?

choices.text: That something is there to be aware of
Whether to keep one's focus on the evidence
Whether to blank out a contradiction
Whether to integrate what one knows

feedback.note: Awareness of reality is not invented by a vote. What one does with that awareness at the conceptual level is chosen.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to chosen or not chosen.

pairs.left: The fact that exists
Whether to identify it without contradiction
Whether to drop the context of a claim
A wish that the fact were otherwise

feedback.note: Choice governs adherence. It does not govern whether reality is what it is.

exercises.prompt: Name the kind of adherence this unit teaches.

feedback.note: The unit's word is volitional. The facts are not automatic products of a wish, and adherence is not impossible.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast this lesson draws.

tokens.text: Reality is not up to a vote

feedback.note: The choice is whether to adhere, not whether the facts may be edited.

exercises.prompt: A person sees a broken gauge and tells himself it is fine so the day stays easy. What failed?

choices.text: The choice to adhere; the gauge reading was not chosen away
The gauge, because awareness creates cracks
Nothing; comfort is a method of logic
Reality, for refusing to match the wish

feedback.note: Evasion is a chosen refusal to identify what one is aware of. It does not change the gauge.

exercises.prompt: Which action is an exercise of the volitional side of objectivity?

choices.text: Holding a conclusion to the evidence when a contradiction appears
Blinking when light hits the eyes
Growing taller
Having a dream one did not stage

feedback.note: Objectivity's volitional part is mental adherence. Reflexes, growth, and unsought dreams are not that method.

exercises.prompt: Match the response to the name that fits this unit.

pairs.left: I will check the contradiction
I will not think about that fact
The fact must change because I prefer another one

feedback.note: Only the first response is volitional adherence. The other two abandon the facts instead of following them.

exercises.prompt: Complete the split.

parts.text: One does not choose the facts. One chooses whether to

feedback.note: Erase, vote, and invent describe failures or substitutes. The objective choice is to adhere.

exercises.prompt: State the choice in order.

tokens.text: choose to identify it by logic
wait for the fact to obey

feedback.note: Awareness supplies the material. The volitional step is identification by the method of logic.

lessons.title: Knowledge in context
lessons.objective: Treat a conclusion as holding in the context of the evidence that supports it, and treat context-dropping as a failure of objectivity.

exercises.prompt: What does it mean, in this unit, to call knowledge contextual?

choices.text: A conclusion is held in the context of the knowledge that supports it
Any sentence is true in every context and in none
Context makes evidence unnecessary
Context means one's mood at the moment of speaking

feedback.note: Contextual does not mean arbitrary. It means the claim stays tied to the evidence and knowledge around it.

exercises.prompt: What is context-dropping?

choices.text: Using a claim apart from the knowledge that gives it its meaning
Adding the relevant evidence before judging
Keeping earlier knowledge in mind
Naming the facts one actually has

feedback.note: Dropping context tears a conclusion away from the conditions under which it was reached.

exercises.prompt: Match each move to contextual or not.

pairs.left: Judge a claim by the evidence that bears on it
Quote a rule while hiding the case it was about
Treat a partial observation as the whole story

feedback.note: Context is the surrounding knowledge a conclusion depends on. Hiding that surround is not objectivity.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit's second claim about knowledge.

feedback.note: The unit calls knowledge contextual and hierarchical. It does not call a human mind omniscient or context-free.

exercises.prompt: Build a contextual judgment.

tokens.text: inside the evidence that supports it
outside every fact that limits it

feedback.note: A contextual claim carries its evidence with it. Stripping the limits is context-dropping.

exercises.prompt: A medicine works for one condition. Someone announces it cures every illness. What went wrong?

choices.text: The context of the result was dropped
Nothing; wider claims are always safer
The original result stopped being a fact
Only the spelling of the drug's name matters

feedback.note: The result stays knowledge of the case that was shown. Extending it without new evidence leaves that context behind.

exercises.prompt: Does contextual knowledge mean one may ignore new evidence?

choices.text: No. The context includes the relevant evidence one has, including new evidence
Yes. Context freezes a conclusion forever
Only if the new evidence is unpleasant
Only until a crowd disagrees

feedback.note: Keeping context means keeping the relevant knowledge, not shielding a conclusion from further facts.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to the error or the practice.

pairs.left: Out of context
In the light of the evidence one has
True with no relation to any knowledge

feedback.note: Objectivity does not ask for a claim that floats free of all knowledge. It asks for a claim held in context.

exercises.prompt: Fill the failure this lesson names.

parts.text: Using a conclusion apart from its evidence is

feedback.note: Adherence, logic, and hierarchy are parts of the standard. Context-dropping is the failure of the contextual part.

exercises.prompt: Which question respects context?

choices.text: True of what, on what evidence?
True of everything, evidence aside?
Pleasing to whom?
Comfortable today?

feedback.note: Asking what the claim is about and what supports it is how one keeps the context in view.

lessons.title: Knowledge in an order
lessons.objective: Treat knowledge as hierarchical: later conclusions rest on earlier ones and cannot replace the base they depend on.

exercises.prompt: What does this unit mean by hierarchical knowledge?

choices.text: Later knowledge rests on earlier knowledge in an order
Every claim is a loose item in a pile of equals
The newest sentence always erases the earlier ones
Social rank decides which claim is basic

feedback.note: Hierarchy is an order of dependence. It is not a pile, a fashion for the latest line, or a social rank.

exercises.prompt: A later conclusion contradicts the earlier knowledge it needed. What follows?

choices.text: The later conclusion cannot stand by destroying its own base
The later conclusion wins because it came second
Both are kept, base or no base
The earlier knowledge is discarded for being earlier

feedback.note: In a hierarchy, the later item depends on the earlier. It cannot refute its base and remain standing.

exercises.prompt: Match each level to its role in the order.

pairs.left: Earlier knowledge a conclusion relies on
A conclusion drawn from that base
Treating every sentence as equally first

feedback.note: First comes the knowledge something rests on. The conclusion comes after, and it does not become a new first by being complex.

exercises.prompt: Complete the pair of traits.

feedback.note: Hierarchical is the unit's word. A flat, baseless, or freely reversed stack is not that order.

exercises.prompt: Build the order of dependence.

feedback.note: Support runs from earlier to later. A later claim that cancels its base has left the hierarchy.

exercises.prompt: Why is a pile of unrelated assertions not objective knowledge?

choices.text: It has no order of what rests on what, so contradictions are not integrated
Only because the pile might be short
Only because the assertions are written down
Because earlier knowledge is always worthless

feedback.note: Objectivity integrates knowledge in an order. A heap does not show what depends on what.

exercises.prompt: Match the attempt to the verdict.

pairs.left: Reduce a conclusion to the knowledge it rests on
Use a late conclusion to deny the earlier knowledge it assumes
Add a new fact and adjust the later claim

feedback.note: Learning can revise a later claim when the base changes. It cannot use the later claim to wipe out the base the claim required.

exercises.prompt: Fill both sides of the summary.

feedback.note: Both words belong. Contextual without an order, or an order with no context, would drop half of the unit summary.

exercises.prompt: Which picture fits the whole unit?

choices.text: Choose to adhere to reality by logic, and hold knowledge in context and in order
Choose a wish, then call the wish a base
Keep context, but contradict the facts on purpose
Stack claims so the latest one needs no earlier knowledge

feedback.note: Objectivity joins the volitional method to knowledge that is both contextual and hierarchical.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the unit in one line.

tokens.text: with knowledge a flat pile of wishes

feedback.note: That is the unit: a chosen adherence, logic as the method, and knowledge held in context and in a hierarchy.
